omar diaz: Morning team / quick one. My spouse just lost employer coverage (layoff) and wants me to add them. Im currently on the HDHP+HSA plan and also put money into a Limited FSA at Open Enrollment. Can I switch to the PPO midyear and move funds from the L-FSA to a general FSA? What paperwork do you need for the spouses loss of coverage?
zoe (People Ops): Sorry to hear about the layoff, @omar. Yes, loss of other coverage is a common QLE that lets you 1) change medical plan and 2) add a dependent. However, HSA eligibility rules and FSA types are separate: you can switch medical plans midyear, but you cannot "convert" Limited FSA to general FSA in many cases unless the plan documents allow it. Well need proof of spouses loss of coverage (termination letter or COBRA notice) showing an event date. Upload within 30 days of the QLE date for retro benefits.
samir (note): (Im adding payroll and benefits notes below)
benefits-bot: @omar Upload docs: 1) Spouse termination or COBRA offer letter (PDF/JPG). 2) Marriage certificate if adding spouse for the first time. Steps: HR Portal -> Benefits -> Report QLE -> Select "Loss of Other Coverage" -> Upload Docs -> Choose action: "Change plan" + "Add spouse". Accepted formats: PDF, PNG, JPG. Max 10MB. Recommended filename: diaz_spouse_term_20260501.pdf
omar diaz: Ok uploaded `diaz_spouse_term_20260501.pdf` and my marriage_cert_2018.pdf via secure upload. If I switch off HDHP does that immediately make me ineligible for HSA contributions? What happens to money already in my HSA?
zoe (People Ops): Good Q. HSA eligibility is determined by the coverage on the payroll deduction effective date. If the medical change is effective the same day your HDHP ends, you become ineligible for new HSA contributions starting that pay period. Money already in your HSA remains yours and stays tax-advantaged; you can still use it for qualified expenses. You cannot contribute to an HSA while covered by a non-HSA-eligible plan (like PPO) or enrolled in a general FSA that covers medical expenses.
sam payroll: Payroll/benefits coordination: 1) If carrier accepts the QLE and sets PPO effective date retro to the event, payroll will adjust premiums retroactively and stop HSA pre-tax deductions starting the effective date. 2) Any HSA contributions already deducted for pay periods after the effective date will be corrected (tax reporting will be adjusted). 3) HSA trustees handle distribution of funds; we do not move money between HSA and FSA.
omar diaz: And the L-FSA? I chose Limited FSA because HDHP+HSA was my plan. If I switch to PPO, can I change election to general FSA midyear?
zoe (People Ops): Most cafeteria plan documents only allow midyear election changes for FSA when there's a corresponding change in status (like dependent loss/gain) and only if plan permits. A switch from HDHP to PPO due to spouse losing coverage is a permissible QLE for changing your medical election, but converting Limited FSA -> General FSA is plan-specific. We will: 1) submit the QLE and request the FSA change on your behalf, 2) benefits admin will check plan rules and reply. If allowed, payroll will prorate the new per-pay contributions; if not allowed, you may keep Limited FSA or stop contributions (depending on plan rules).
payroll-bot: If FSA election change is approved: contributions will be recalculated pro-rata based on the effective date. Example: `annual election / remaining pay periods = new per-pay amount`. Any over-contributions may be adjusted on the next payroll. Tax implications: general FSA dollars are pre-tax and may affect taxable wages going forward.
omar diaz: Timeline? I uploaded docs at 2026-05-02. If approved, when would PPO coverage start and HSA stop?
zoe (People Ops): Carriers often set effective dates either retro to the QLE event date (if docs within 30 days) or to the date they process the change. Typical flow: verification 2-4 business days, carrier effective date depends on carrier rules but often retro to the loss-of-coverage date if submitted within 30 days. We'll confirm specific effective dates once benefits admin responds.
benefits-bot: Case created: QLE-2026-884. Verification ETA 3 business days. Portal path to change plan: Benefits -> Report a Life Event -> Loss of Other Coverage -> Actions: Change medical plan + Add dependent -> Confirm -> Review payroll impact.
sam payroll: FYI: If PPO goes into effect retro, payroll will: 1) reverse HSA pre-tax deductions after that date, 2) apply new PPO premium. Expect a reconciliation line on next paycheck +/- one additional cycle depending on timing. Keep copies of uploaded docs for your records.
omar diaz: Thanks all. If the FSA change is denied, can I stop L-FSA contributions and open a general FSA in the next Open Enrollment?
zoe (People Ops): Yes, you can always change elections at next Open Enrollment. If denied now, we can stop L-FSA contributions prospectively if your plan allows a midyear stop for this QLE; benefits admin will confirm. We'll follow up in this thread after verification. :thumbsup:
